title: Permission to Operate: Inspection, Approval Validity and Meter Requirements by Net Energy Metering Rider
content:
After approval, a Net Energy Metering system needs permission to operate before it exports under its rider. The rider sets whether a company witness inspection comes first, how long an approval stays valid, how quickly permission is issued, and whether a bidirectional meter must be in service.

| Rider | Witness inspection before permission to operate | Approval validity (months) | Business days to issue permission after a passed inspection, or after the installation notice where no inspection is required | Bidirectional meter in service before permission to operate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering | Not required | 12 | 5 | Required |
| Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering | Not required | 12 | 5 | Required |
| Rider NBT-R Residential Net Billing Tariff | Not required | 12 | 5 | Required |
| Rider NBT-C Commercial Net Billing Tariff | Required | 12 | 10 | Required |
| Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering | Required | 18 | 10 | Required |
| Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff | Required | 24 | 15 | Required |

## Points of the table

- Under the three residential riders no witness inspection is required, and the 5 business days run from the installation notice.
- Under the three business riders the business days run from a passed inspection.
- A bidirectional meter must be in service at the address under every rider.
- Approval validity is 12 months except under Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering (18 months) and Rider NBT-L Large Customer Net Billing Tariff (24 months).
